title: Priya's fix for the review renderer
brief: Priya has been learning alongside you and sent her first security fix for review. Her description: "Swapped innerHTML for textContent. I think that's it?" Be as honest in your review as you would want someone to be in theirs.

reasons.text: It should HTML-encode the body instead of using textContent.
It does not strip <script> tags out of the review.
Reviews with bold text or links will lose their formatting.

reasonExplanations.encode: textContent already does what encoding is for -- the browser never parses the text as markup
reasonExplanations.script: nothing needs stripping when nothing is parsed; a <script> tag in textContent is just characters on screen
reasonExplanations.formatting: Aurora's reviews are plain text by design, so there is no formatting to lose -- that is a product question, not a security one

hints: Ask what the browser does with a string given to textContent. Does it ever look inside it for tags?
Not every review needs changes requested. Sometimes the fix is simply right.
